how the encoder works

The encoder is composed of a stack of N = 6 identical layers. Each layer has two sub-layers: a multi-head self-attention mechanism and a simple, position-wise fully connected feed-forward network. 

In a self-attention layer, all of the keys, values, and queries come from the same place, in this case, the output of the previous layer in the encoder. Each position in the encoder can attend to all positions in the previous layer of the encoder.

What is the main idea behind the Transformer model?

The main idea behind the Transformer model is to replace traditional recurrent neural networks (RNNs) with self-attention mechanisms, allowing for parallel computation of hidden representations for all input and output positions, and reducing sequential computation.
What tasks were used to evaluate the Transformer?
English-to-German translation on the development set, newstest2013 and English-to-French newstest2014 tests.
What BLEU score did the Transformer achieve on English-to-German translation?
The Transformer (big) model achieved a BLEU score of 28.4 on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task.
Why is self-attention better than recurrent networks?

Self-attention is better than recurrent networks because it connects all positions with a constant number of sequentially executed operations, whereas a recurrent layer requires O(n) sequential operations.
Why is multi-head attention useful?

Multi-head attention allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions. This is not possible with a single attention head, as averaging inhibits this.
How long did the base Transformer model take to train?

The base models were trained for a total of 100,000 steps, and each training step took about 0.4 seconds. Therefore, the base models took 100,000 * 0.4 = 40,000 seconds to train. Converting this to hours, we get 40,000 / 3600 = 11.11 hours.
What value of dropout was used in the base model?
The base model used a dropout rate of Pdrop = 0.1.

What role does positional encoding play?

Positional encoding is used to inject information about the relative or absolute position of the tokens in the sequence, allowing the model to make use of the order of the sequence since it contains no recurrence and no convolution.
Why are convolutions less efficient for long dependencies?

Convolutions are generally more expensive than recurrent layers, by a factor of k. Additionally, a single convolutional layer with kernel width k<n does not connect all pairs of input and output positions, requiring a stack of O(n/k) convolutional layers in the case of contiguous kernels, or O(logk(n)) in the case of dilated convolutions, increasing the length of the longest paths between any two positions in the network.

How does scaled dot-product attention avoid small gradients?
To counteract the effect of extremely small gradients, the dot products in scaled dot-product attention are scaled by 1√dk.
Summarize the reasons the authors prefer self-attention over convolutional layers.

The authors prefer self-attention over convolutional layers because self-attention layers are faster than recurrent layers when the sequence length n is smaller than the representation dimensionality d, which is most often the case with sentence representations used by state-of-the-art models in machine translations.
